coverage_notes: Viewed all registered anchors on PDF pp.4 and 6, plus title p.1, composition/heat treatment p.2 and hydrogen-reference text p.3. Figure 3 was enlarged and actually viewed; crowded low-addition symbols remain ambiguous. No registry values or IDs were changed.
shared_qualifications: C12 (conditional): E(mV vs SCE)=1000 E(V vs NHE)-244. The paper explicitly states normal hydrogen reference (PDF p.3). The 25 C calomel value +0.244 V vs SHE is tabulated by HORIBA: https://www.horiba.com/twn/water-quality/support/electrochemistry/the-basis-of-ph/electrical-potential-of-reference-electrode/ . Comparison assumes the target saturated-calomel scale is at 25 C and NHE is the common hydrogen scale. Reference-electrode temperature/calibration is not specified; solution temperature alone does not establish it. The constant was not fitted to CRA targets.

The 18Cr-14Ni base is Cr 17.93, Ni 14.38, C 0.036 wt.% (PDF p.2). Table I supplies supplementary contents in wt.%; starred Ce/Re/Mo contents are based on charge. Nominal 5% labels are distinguished from Table I V 4.75% and Si 4.74%.

Table 3 annealed (2 h at 650 C) and quenched (1150 C, water quenched) results are distinct. Quenched V and Si >1.50 V are bounds, not exact thresholds. The quenched baseline and high-V bound have no corresponding row in this CSV.

obs_006/Ce 0.2% is about 0.66 V in the registry and visible figure, giving conditionally 416 mV versus CRA 400; identity is independently supported but potential agreement is discrepant. obs_007 registry 0.51 V lies below the visible approximately 0.52 V Ce marker; CRA 279 mV corresponds conditionally to 0.523 V. Both registry readings are preserved, with discrepancies explicit.

Partial obs_024/025/026 retain their unresolved cluster-series assignments. Compatible Nb 0.92, Ta 1.00 and Nb 1.30 rows remain candidates; numerical agreement does not resolve the faint series. Partial low-Si obs_015 is assessed, but no Si 1.45% row is supplied.

The annealed Mo breakdown is associated in the source with grain-boundary/intergranular attack, rather than unqualified pitting. Si near nominal 5% has an alpha phase in the source (p.2); CRA 383 only says austenitic. Qualifications are retained without excluding the registered outcomes.
